A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAGIC research work. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on Fitzpatrick17k and SCIN, synthetic-image evaluations, few-shot results and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PAD-UFES-20 experiments, evaluator and backbone comparisons, checklist-granularity results and clinician assessment of GPT-4o descriptions.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same Textual Inversion/LoRA preparation, image-to-image generation, preference processing, RFT/DPO objectives and augmentation procedure. MedGemma and nine-criterion checklists are tested as alternative configurations of the existing framework; no new algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Fitzpatrick17k and SCIN coverage, v2 evaluates PAD-UFES-20 on four overlapping conditions: ACK, BCC, MEL and SCC. It also introduces an internal dataset of 100 clinically confirmed real images for assessing GPT-4o descriptions, expanding both the clinical data sources and evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: The original real-only, T2I, I2I and MAGIC-RFT/DPO comparisons remain unchanged. Table 5 adds an evaluated feedback alternative: MAGIC using MedGemma-4B is compared with MAGIC using GPT-4o. This is a limited comparator addition within the framework, rather than a new competing augmentation pipeline.

E3.justification: Original splits and training settings remain unchanged. Added protocols include dermatologist scoring of descriptions for 100 real images, comparing evaluators on the same 1,024 image pairs, testing ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16, and using nine-criterion checklists. Table 13 inconsistently labels the retained structured baseline as seven criteria, whereas the text specifies five; this does not establish an actual baseline-setting change.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of evaluator reliability, evaluator choice, backbone dependence and checklist granularity. Figure 8 adds qualitative diversity examples within and across anatomical sites, and Appendix G adds failure analysis, including a medicine-powder misinterpretation. The original feedback-volume, synthetic-ratio and coarse-versus-structured ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different random seeds in Appendix A.4. However, v2's new NeurIPS checklist states that all experiments were repeated for three rounds. This introduces contradictory run-count reporting without establishing an actual reduction in runs. No confidence intervals, error-bar definitions or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4 and SCIN results are unchanged. New results include PAD-UFES-20 real/MAGIC accuracies of 63.02/70.65 for ResNet-18 and 67.88/73.85 for DINOv2, MedGemma-based accuracies of 36.97 and 54.19, and nine-criterion accuracies of 39.39 and 55.88. Additional backbone results and 86% of clinician-rated descriptions meeting at least three criteria further expand the evidence; these are newly reported experiments, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the MDP formulation, trajectory-preference assumption and score-processing rules are unchanged. The new task-centric alignment and hallucination discussions are conceptual explanations, not new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The clinical augmentation claims and headline gains of 9.02 and 13.89 percentage points remain. The abstract and conclusion add an explicit contribution framed as task-centric alignment for specialized domains, and the conclusion emphasizes flexibility across MLLM evaluators. This broadens the framing without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of constrained-checklist hallucination resistance, GPT-4o versus MedGemma performance, backbone-dependent benefits, diminishing returns from checklist detail and sources of image diversity. Appendices G–H identify concrete visual-assessment failures and qualify privacy claims by acknowledging absent formal guarantees. The original general limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: Table 12 adds parameter counts and pretraining datasets, and the nine checklist attributes are named. Existing hyperparameters, prompts and detailed five-criterion checklists remain unchanged. The abstract now explicitly advertises code at the existing repository, but the new conference checklist says code will be released upon acceptance, leaving availability inconsistently documented.

R1.justification: The earlier references and related-work comparisons are retained. Added citations cover MedGemma, prompt tuning, continual learning, eSkinHealth and other recent work. Appendix E connects several of these to future extensions, without substantially revising MAGIC's relationship to existing augmentation and feedback-alignment methods.

P1.justification: Most existing introduction, related-work, method and experimental prose remains unchanged, as does the main section order. Editing concentrates on the expanded abstract and conclusion, added explanatory subsections, appendix organization, acknowledgments and the appended NeurIPS checklist. The revision primarily extends the existing narrative rather than extensively rewriting it.

P2.justification: v2 adds an alignment-score pie chart, a diversity image grid, evaluator and PAD-UFES-20 tables, and backbone/granularity tables that partly redisplay earlier results. It also regroups appendix displays and reflows the long checklist table. Earlier Figures 5–6 are retained as Figures 6–7, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The clinician-reviewed description study and MedGemma comparison directly examine evaluator reliability and dependence that v1 left less tested. Additional dataset/backbone evaluations and concrete failure/privacy discussions also strengthen the paper. These gains are limited by sparse PAD-UFES-20 protocol documentation and new inconsistencies concerning checklist size, run counts and code availability. The retained core results and lack of uncertainty estimates support a limited overall improvement.
